title: Effects of Health and Environmental Messages in the Context of Increasing Whole Grain Consumption: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
summary:
Environmental crises pose a major threat to health. Because of dynamic relationships between human, animal and environmental health, individuals contribute significantly to environmental problems, while environmental problems affect human health and well-being, implying that environmental and health issues cannot be considered separately. Individual lifestyle measures (e.g. a healthy and sustainable nutrition) offer benefits for personal well-being and act as health-promoting behaviors while reducing one's ecological footprint. One way to respond to these challenges is to promote behavior that is both sustainable and health-promoting. Accordingly, it is important to investigate how people can be motivated to change their behavior, how people differ in the process of behavior change  and which mechanisms underlie this change. This will be investigated using the consumption of whole grain products, as whole grains offer both health benefits and represent a sustainable way of eating. A good way to motivate people to change their behavior is to use app-based notifications. These can be used to send people daily information and reminders. 
In this study, participants are contacted daily via a study app and respond to questions regarding their whole-grain-related intentions, attitudes, and behaviors across three weeks. During the last two weeks, participants also receive information messages about whole grains. These are different for the three study groups: The first group receives neutral messages, the second group receives information on health benefits of whole grains and the third group receives information on positive environmental effects of whole grains.
conditions: Whole grain consumption as a healthy and environmentally friendly eating behavior

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
To take part, participants must have a smartphone and be willing to install the study app. They must also have sufficient knowledge of German to be able to read and understand the study information and answer the questions.
Exclusion criteria:
People who do not have a smartphone or are not willing to install the study app. People who do not have sufficient knowledge of German to be able to read and understand the study information and answer the questions.
